# BACTERIAL MENINGITIS WITH GRAM-NEGATIVE DIPLOCOCCI SUGGESTING NEISSERIA

# MENINGITIDIS

Once a diagnosis of acute bacterial meningitis is considered likely,
antimicrobials should be initiated as soon as possible. Two blood cultures
should be drawn. Lumbar puncture (LP) should be performed in nearly all patients
to obtain cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) for establishing diagnosis and determining
infectious organism/susceptibility. Adjust antimicrobial regimen to optimize
therapy and treatment duration based on pathogen once isolated.

If meningococcal meningitis is identified, antimicrobial prophylaxis should be
considered for close contacts. Contact Infectious Diseases/Epidemiology for
advice and assistance.

# Consult Infectious Diseases

# Empiric Treatment

Preferred:

[Ceftriaxone 2 gm IV q12h \($\) M](psjizid-ceftriaxone-2gm-iv-q12h)

Alternative:

[Assessment of beta-lactam reaction](orz-gtx-abx-beta-lactam-reaction-pdf)

[Meropenem 2 gm IV q8h \($$\) R,O](psjizid-meropenem-2gm-iv-q8h)
